title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 63–64 of the 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}' notes). D_d is the analytic (orbifold) space attached to curves with d double points, i.e. the boundary stratum of codimension d of the Deligne–Mumford compactification, or its normalisation. D*_d is the open part, the complement of the divisors Θ_d coming from deeper strata. Over D_d there is a group G_d, an 'extended' torus twisted by S_d: fibrewise (C^*)^d, or C^d as a monoid, the product of the smoothing parameters of the d nodes. There is also a G_d-torsor P_d, essentially the punctured normal 'tubular' data. The local system T_d of the π_1 = H_1 of its fibres is a twisted Z^d: the lattice of Dehn twists around the d vanishing cycles.

On p.63 Grothendieck forms flag spaces D_{d_0,...,d_r} (d_0 ≥ ... ≥ d_r). Each is a finite étale cover of D_{d_0}, parametrising flags of type d_* in the set of d_0 nodes. Their disjoint union is D_{Δ_r}. Contravariant functoriality in increasing maps of simplices makes this a semi-simplicial ('1/2-simplicial') analytic space D_•, essentially the nerve of the boundary stratification.

This page does three things.
(206) It defines D*_• as the inverse image of D*_0 = ⊔_d D*_d under the 'first component' maps D_{d_0,...,d_r} → D_{d_0}. These are induced by the vertex inclusion [0] → [r], 0 ↦ 0, i.e. forgetting the flag.
(207)–(208) It pulls back the G_{d_0}-torsor P_{d_0} and the group G_{d_0} along the same map, obtaining P_{d_0..d_r} and G_{d_0..d_r}, with starred versions restricted to D*_{d_0..d_r}.
(209) It asserts a 2-cartesian square of fundamental groupoids. On top: Π̂_{d_*} = Π_1 P*_{d_*} → Π̂_{d_0} = Π_1 P*_{d_0}. On the bottom: Π_1 D_{d_*} → Π_1 D_{d_0}.

The next page interprets the vertical maps as extensions by the twisted lattices T_{d_0} (Dehn-twist subgroups). It then assembles everything over the semi-simplicial base (G_{Δ_r}, P_{Δ_r}, T_{Δ_r}).

Purpose: build a semi-simplicial model of the 'homotopy type at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, i.e. the deleted tubular neighbourhood of the boundary. The model consists of torus-torsor bundles over the flag-nerve of the stratification, with their fundamental groupoids. These are extensions of the strata's π_1 by Dehn-twist lattices, presumably to be glued into a description of the profinite / Teichmüller structure at infinity.
errors: The square (209) is 2-cartesian because D_{d_0..d_r} → D_{d_0} is a finite étale covering, and the fundamental groupoid of a pullback along a covering is the 2-fibre product. Fine.

Minor inconsistency: the top row uses P* (lying over D*), but the bottom row is written Π_1 D_{d_0..d_r} and 'Π D_{d_0}' (subscript 1 omitted). Logically the bottom row should be Π_1 D*_{...}, or the top should be Π_1 P. The margin on p.64 ('π_1 de D_{d_0} & de D*_{d_0}?') shows Grothendieck was himself unsure here.
In (206) the morphism is written 'o: D_* → D_*'. It should be D_• → D_0 (i.e. D_{Δ_r} → D_{Δ_0}), induced by the vertex 0 ∈ [0,r].
Carried from p.63: in (204) the index set should be N^{r+1}, not N^r.

ideas.what: Semi-simplicial space of flags of boundary strata (nested sets of nodes), each term finite étale over the open strata
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial resolution / nerve of a normal-crossings stratification; for M_g it corresponds to the boundary complex (tropical moduli space / curve complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge III simplicial resolutions); Harvey (curve complex, 1981); boundary complex of M_g: Chan–Galatius–Payne (2018–21)

ideas.what: Pulling back the torus torsor of smoothing parameters (normal 'tubular' data) and its group along the flag maps
ideas.modern_name: Deleted tubular neighbourhood of boundary strata as a torus-bundle; log structure / tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kato / Illusie (log geometry); Ihara–Nakamura (Teichmüller groupoid at infinity)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and boundary structure only informally

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the punctured neighbourhood of a stratum as an extension of the stratum's π_1 by a twisted Z^d (Dehn twists), compatible under 2-cartesian squares with flags
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser/normaliser of a multicurve in the mapping class group as an extension by the free abelian group of Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical mapping-class-group theory (Ivanov, Birman); profinite version: Nakamura, Boggi

missed.claim: The construction models the homotopy type at infinity of M_{g,ν} as a semi-simplicial object over the flag nerve of the boundary stratification, with torus torsors (Dehn-twist lattices) as fibres. This anticipates the 'boundary complex / tropical moduli' viewpoint, augmented by torus-bundle data, i.e. a full hocolim model of the link at infinity rather than just its dual complex.
missed.quote: On a donc un diagramme 2-cartésien de groupoïdes ... Π̂_{d_0…d_r} = Π_1 P*_{d_0,…,d_r}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work (Chan–Galatius–Payne, and work on Teichmüller groupoids at infinity in anabelian geometry) treats either the dual complex or profinite boundary groups separately. A combined semi-simplicial torsor/groupoid model, intended for the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting, is not standard in print. It is, however, a natural construction that experts would recognise.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine setup step: pulling back torsors and groups along flag coverings and noting a 2-cartesian square. The overall programme (semi-simplicial model of the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}) is interesting, but this page contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: First line probably reads 'nous définissons tout de suite' (or similar), not 'un peu à définir tout de suite'.
'Gal-torseur' in (207) is 'G_d-torseur' (torsor under G_{d_0}); the same in the inserted heading 'G_d-torseurs'.
'la morphisme' → 'le morphisme'; the arrow 'o : D_* → D_*' is from the semi-simplicial D_• to D_0.
'(transposé de ...)' refers to the inclusion of vertex 0 into the chain 0→1→2→…→r, i.e. the 'premier composant' map.
The garbled line '[-[?]-]{+de A[?]+} des torseurs sous les groupes [?], analytiques [?] (étendus)' likely reads roughly 'c.-à-d. des torseurs sous les groupes analytiques (étendus)'.
In (209) the bottom-right is written 'Π D_{d_0}' (subscript 1 missing in the original).
